content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a question about the data log feature. I need to save the date and time whenever an input turns on or off. Is this possible through the data log function? Thank you in advance, [user_name]
Yes, this is possible. Every entry created by the data log feature includes a time and date stamp. However, you should wait at least 500 ms between each log entry to ensure proper logging.

Thank you for your quick response. My next question: how can I keep these values accessible later using the access tool? The device is installed in a location where the SD card cannot be easily reached.
The [product_name] Access Tool cannot read or process a data log file directly. You either create a data log on an SD card, or you use the Access Tool separately.

So, is it not possible to read the information stored by the data log function remotely? Can we instead store the data as variables? From what I’ve seen, it appears possible to read variables through the access tool. [url]

Refer to section 2.4 (Getting [product_name] Variable Value) in the help document. There are two different concepts: - Data log ([product_name]) - A log file produced by the access tool The data log is a file generated and saved automatically to the SD card by the device. The access tool produces its own log file. Instructions for creating a log file using the access tool are found in section 2.4 (page 15) of the help document.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are attempting to track when a digital input switches states using the data log feature. Responses confirm that each data log entry is timestamped, but emphasize allowing a 500 ms gap between entries for reliable operation. A challenge is highlighted: the [product_name] Access Tool does not support direct processing of data log files, making remote access difficult when physical SD card access is unavailable. Users discuss possible workarounds, such as using variables, and consult documentation for alternative solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to accurately record the on/off times of a digital input and remotely retrieve this data without needing physical SD card access, ideally by using the [product_name] Access Tool.
